stories.title: Former Labour TD Michael Conaghan dies aged 81
stories.summary: Former Labour Party TD and Lord Mayor of Dublin Michael Conaghan has died at the age of 81. Mr Conaghan was elected to the Dáil for Dublin South Central in 2011, serving one term before stepping away prior to the 2016 General Election. The Donegal native took the second of two Labour seats in the constituency alongside Eric Byrne on a memorable day for the party at the 2011 election. He served 20 years as a councillor on Dublin City Council after his election in 1991, topping the poll on three occasions in the Ballyfermot ward.

The export boom has been propelled further this year by increased demand for Chinese data-processing equipment and related components, as companies rush to build artificial intelligence capacity. Exports climbed 23.9% year-on-year last month, the General Administration of Customs (GAC) reported, compared with a 23% forecast by Bloomberg.

stories.summary: A US Senate committee has voted to hold Dr Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress after the country's former top infectious disease official refused to answer questions about his handling of the Covid-19 pandemic. The Republican-led Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee approved a referral pushed by its Republican Chair Rand Paul of Kentucky, a longtime Fauci antagonist. The vote followed a hearing last week where Dr Fauci, who is 85 and retired in 2022, invoked the Fifth Amendment more than 100 times. Dr Fauci, who led the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases for 38 years, became the face of the US pandemic response and a primary target of anger over measures taken against a virus that killed more than 1.1 million Americans.

stories.title: Wigan and Warrington bring Super League action to Dublin
stories.summary: Warrington Wolves and Wigan Warriors will make history next year when they contest the first-ever Super League fixture to be played in Ireland. The two fierce rivals will meet at the newly redeveloped Laya Arena in Dublin on Saturday 24 April 2027, 5.30pm kick-off, taking one of Rugby League's biggest fixtures to the Irish capital for a landmark occasion. The fixture continues Super League's recent run of blockbuster overseas showcases and follows Warrington and Wigan's historic meeting in Las Vegas in 2025. Laya Arena, in the Royal Dublin Society's (RDS) comlex in Ballsbridge, has undergone a €52m transformation and officially reopens today with the Dublin Horse Show. It is also the home ground of Leinster Rugby Union.

stories.summary: We feed them, cuddle them, and live alongside them, but how much do you really know about your cat? stories.title: Man faces trial over gun possession outside garda station
stories.summary: A 21-year-old man who allegedly brandished a handgun outside a Dublin garda station, before a young boy later fired it in the area, has been sent forward for trial. Josh Larkin was charged with weapons offences for possessing a black handgun and producing it in the course of a dispute, at Gateway Crescent outside Ballymun Garda station in the city's north side on 28 April. Unemployed Mr Larkin, of Poppintree Crescent, Ballymun, also faces a connected charge for possessing cannabis at Sillogue Park on the same date. On 30 April, bail was set at €20,000, with a €6,500 cash lodgement required, and he remains in custody.

stories.title: Tensions cool between EU and Spain over crisis in Ceuta
stories.summary: The Government will likely breathe a sigh of relief as the political temperature surrounding Spain's handling of the migrant crisis in Ceuta cools after some fractious exchanges among EU member states in recent days. Minister for Justice Jim O'Callaghan was forced to convene an emergency meeting of EU interior and justice ministers after the images of over 50,000 people swimming across the border from Morocco to the Spanish North African territory pushed immigration to the top of the agenda for Ireland's EU Presidency. This morning's meeting came with Spain on the offensive - expressing annoyance at the lack of solidarity from other EU members and accusing some of turning the crisis into an attack on its Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. Others wanted swift action against Madrid - with Italy and Denmark last week advocating for Spain to be suspended from the Schengen free-travel area over the crisis; 20 other countries joined them in saying the EU should continue pressing their tough line on immigration, seemingly at odds with Spain's open stance on migration.

stories.title: Airbnb tops revenue estimates on demand, World Cup boost
stories.summary: Vacation rental company Airbnb has beaten second-quarter revenue estimates, helped by strong global demand for travel and a boost from first time users during the FIFA World Cup hosted in the US, Canada and Mexico. Travel companies, including online agencies Expedia and Booking have benefited from the recently concluded World Cup. Airbnb noted that its North American bookings during the second quarter recorded the highest growth in almost three years. Shares of the San Francisco-based company rose 10.8% in extended trading. "We've delivered some of the strongest results in years," Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky said on an earnings call. "More new guests are trying Airbnb than we've seen in years."

stories.title: Israel charges settler in killing of Palestinian activist
stories.summary: Prosecutors charged an Israeli settler in the killing of Palestinian activist Awdah Hathaleen in the occupied West Bank, the first such indictment since the outbreak of the Gaza war in 2023, activists say. "Yinon Eliya Levi (33), from Ma'on, has been charged with allegedly firing toward an area where people were present during a confrontation that developed over earthworks on private land, causing the death of the late Awdah Hathaleen," Israel's ministry of justice said on X. "The Southern District Prosecutor's Office has filed an indictment against him... on charges of reckless manslaughter, trespassing, and willful property damage." Mr Hathaleen, an activist who took part in the production of the Oscar-winning documentary "No Other Land", was killed in July 2025 during a settler attack on his village of Umm al-Khair, in the southern West Bank.

stories.title: Collins and McClean are more alike than they realise
stories.summary: Derry City have reached the point where the noise around the club has become louder than the football being played on the pitch. Tiernan Lynch is gone, James McClean has been firing messages into the public domain, and Roddy Collins has been standing on the other side returning them with interest. It's been entertaining from the outside, but for a club with the so-called ambition of Derry’s, with the investment and support into both the playing squad and the club itself, it could not be allowed to continue. Lynch’s departure was necessary. His work at Larne, where he won back-to-back league titles and took the club into the league phase of European competition, is to be applauded.

stories.title: Something for the Weekend: Reevah's cultural picks
stories.summary: NI Music Prize-nominated indie-pop artist Reevah (AKA Aoife Boyle) has just released her introspective new single, The Hardest Part. The acclaimed singer-songwriter from Derry won kudos for her debut album Daylight Savings - these days, she's fusing heart-on-sleeve pop with country balladry, with winning results. I really loved Hamnet, directed by Chloé Zhao. I went to see this in the cinema when it came out. Jessie Buckley's performance was brilliant: raw, emotional, and completely captivating. It's one of those films that stays with you long after you’ve watched it, and those are always the stories I connect with most. I found myself thinking about it for days afterwards. I’m a huge fan of CMAT and her EURO-COUNTRY album. Much like the music I write, and my latest single, I love that blend of country and indie-pop, especially when it's rooted in great storytelling. I'm always drawn to songs that have something to say. Like the rest of the world, I'm also completely here for Olivia Dean! Alongside that, I'm constantly listening to great Irish artists like Joshua Burnside, Alana Henderson, Fontaines D.C., CHALK, Sorcha Richardson and Soda Blonde, to name just a few.

stories.title: Meta ordered to pay $567m in US child safety ruling
stories.summary: A New Mexico state court has ordered Meta to pay $567 million (€492 million) into a teen mental health fund and change how its platforms function ⁠for young users after finding the company is to blame for harming children's wellbeing. Judge Bryan Biedscheid in Santa Fe ruled the company had created a public nuisance in New Mexico, siding with Attorney General Raúl Torrez, a Democrat. Mr Torrez had accused the social media company of designing products to addict young users and failing to protect children from sexual exploitation on its platforms. The ruling comes five months after a New Mexico jury in an earlier phase of the case ordered Meta to pay $375 million (€325 million) after finding it violated consumer protection law by misrepresenting the safety of Facebook and Instagram for young users.

stories.summary: A coroner has warned that there is no safe level for consuming cocaine following the death from the drug of a hospital chef, described as "hard working" and "football crazy" by his family. Keith McGivern, aged 49, of St Anthony's Road, Rialto, Dublin 8 was found dead in the bedroom of his home on 14 October 2025. A sitting of Dublin District Coroner’s Court heard concern about Mr McGivern’s welfare was raised after he failed to show up at the Coombe Hospital where he had worked for almost 20 years. A sister of the deceased said she had been contacted by one of her brother’s work colleagues when he uncharacteristically did not come to work for two days in a row.

stories.title: Hip surgery for woman after mother confronted Taoiseach
stories.summary: A 19-year-old woman with cerebral palsy, a dysplastic hip, a twisted femur and a retroverted pelvis is to receive specialised surgery in the US following years of campaigning by her family. In September of last year, Antoinette Burke confronted Taoiseach Micheál Martin on his way into a Fianna Fáil think-in at the Rochestown Park Hotel in Co Cork. Ms Burke told Mr Martin that her daughter, Katie Byrne, had been waiting for surgery for 15 years. She claimed that if her daughter had received surgery as a child, she would not need a hip replacement now, an operation which can only be carried out at the Paley Orthopaedic and Spine Institute in Florida.

stories.title: Diageo CEO to cut costs by $1 billion amid low growth
stories.summary: Diageo's new chief executive Dave Lewis has today unveiled a $1 billion restructuring plan, turning to aggressive cost-cutting in order to reset performance as the world's top spirits maker anticipates years of low growth. Investors welcomed the overhaul as a sign that Lewis was moving quickly to tackle years of stagnant or falling sales, sending shares in the Guinness and Johnnie Walker whisky maker up as much as 11% to a more than five-month high. The stock later pared gains to trade 6.5% higher - on track for its best day since November 2020 if gains hold. The spirits industry has been struggling to chart a path back to growth as people have changed what, where and how much they drink.

stories.title: Kilkenny on learning from Belichick & Dublin's potential
stories.summary: The sun shone brightly overhead on what would be the last day in the blue of Dublin for Ciarán Kilkenny. Perhaps it was fitting the old rivals Kerry provided the opposition. The page, when it did turn on the final chapter, had marked down a win for the Kingdom. That was over three weeks ago. An All-Ireland semi-final not without controversy, with a few contentious calls going the way of the green and gold. Still, Kilkenny, though, has few regrets as to how the denouement unfolded. After all it was a glorious career, with eight All-Ireland medals in his pocket. Throughout his career, Kilkenny has made no secret of his love for American sports and the Castleknock native is ambassador for the upcoming Aer Lingus College Football Classic at the Aviva Stadium on 29 August. At a media event ahead of the game between Texas Christian University's Horned Frogs and University of North Carolina’s Tar Heels, the now former Dubs star always had it in his mind that 2026 would be his last season wearing the blue.
